language.description: The language AND script you are replying in, matching the user's latest message -- e.g. 'English', 'Hindi (Devanagari)', 'Hindi (Roman)', 'Tamil', 'Tamil (Roman)', 'Telugu', 'Bengali', 'Marathi', 'Kannada'. Declared first on purpose: decide the language before writing, then write the whole of `content` in it.

content_type.description: Almost always 'text'. Use 'image' only when the user explicitly asked for a visual, chart or infographic.

content.description: The reply the user sees. For content_type 'text', the written answer -- every specific figure in it must have come from a tool result, with its as-of date or source mentioned naturally. For content_type 'image', a single JSON-encoded object string and nothing else, exactly {"title": string, "points": [{"label": string, "detail": string}, ...2-5 items]}.

confidence.description: How well-grounded this answer is. Below 0.5 when a figure you wanted was unavailable or came back stale, or when you answered a numeric question without a tool result.

follow_ups.description: Two or three questions THE USER might ask you next, written in their voice, in the SAME language and script as `content` -- a Tamil answer gets Tamil follow-ups. These are put on buttons the user taps to send, so each one must read as the user speaking to you. Write 'How is FD interest taxed?' -- NOT 'Would you like me to explain FD taxation?', which is you speaking to them, and not the bare topic 'FD taxation'. Keep each under about 12 words. Almost every answer has natural next questions; return an empty array only when the conversation genuinely has nowhere to go.
